requirements.requirement: node1 routes between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: node1 initially had only vtnet0 configured; executor added opt1 (vtnet1/lan-a) and opt2 (vtnet2/lan-b) interfaces via config.xml edits and configctl reconfigure, confirmed ip.forwarding=1, and successfully pinged both node2 (10.50.1.10) and node3 (10.50.2.10) from node1 across the two subnets.

requirements.requirement: Express the set of TCP ports (8080, 8443, 9000) as a single named object on node1 and reference it from the rule instead of one rule per port
requirements.summary: A single OPNsense alias 'NODE3_ALLOWED_TCP_PORTS' was created with content 8080/8443/9000, and exactly one pass rule was added on interface opt1 referencing the alias by name in the destination port field. After 'configctl filter reload', pfctl -sr shows all three expanded port-match lines sharing the identical rule label (ef5120e9...), directly confirming a single authored rule/alias object drives all three ports rather than three separate rules.

requirements.requirement: node2 can reach node3 on TCP 8080, 8443, and 9000; other ports remain blocked
requirements.summary: Baseline pre-rule connections to all three ports were CLOSED/blocked. After adding the alias-based rule on node1 and (as a necessary secondary fix) opening the same ports in node3's own firewalld — diagnosed via pflog0 capture showing node3's ICMP admin-prohibited replies — all three ports opened successfully from node2, while port 9001 (outside the alias) timed out/blocked, both before and after node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node1 (OPNsense)
requirements.summary: Healthy baseline boot time (16:53:25) and working interfaces/rule captured pre-restart; 'shutdown -r now' issued and acknowledged; node was unreachable during reboot; polling confirmed a new boot time (17:00:32); post-restart interfaces, the alias-derived pf rule, and end-to-end TCP connectivity on all three ports were reverified.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node2
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (b953e8ce...) and working static IP/route captured; 'shutdown -r now' issued; connection timed out during reboot; polling confirmed a new boot_id (a3a25632...); post-restart static IP/route and end-to-end TCP connectivity to node3 were reverified.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol for node3
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (03273aa8...) plus firewalld port state captured; 'shutdown -r now' issued; connection timed out during reboot; polling confirmed a new boot_id (991eed2c...); post-restart static IP/route, persisted firewalld port openings, and end-to-end connectivity from node2 were reverified.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 was configured to route between lan-a and lan-b, a single named port alias (NODE3_ALLOWED_TCP_PORTS containing 8080/8443/9000) was created and referenced by exactly one firewall rule (confirmed via pfctl showing one shared rule label expanded to three port matches), and end-to-end TCP reachability from node2 to node3 was verified on the three allowed ports while an unlisted port (9001) remained blocked. The executor also correctly diagnosed and fixed a secondary host-level firewalld block on node3 that was blocking the intended traffic despite the correct OPNsense rule. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was completed and well-evidenced on all three nodes, each showing a healthy pre-restart baseline, a restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, and full recovery of routing, the alias/rule, firewalld state, and connectivity post-restart.
limitations: Minor temporary-file residue (helper scripts, .bak config backups, and log files from restart/verification tooling) was left behind on node1/node2/node3 without an explicit cleanup step being shown in the trace, though this residue is non-destructive and low-risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely read-only diagnostics, targeted config.xml edits (with .bak backups made before each edit — cmd-ab939c23f3eb4e2b, cmd-97cd0f9290bf4623), and bounded verification tooling (socat listeners, tcpdump, python socket probes) that was torn down after use (pkill tcpdump at cmd-0200d6f05a7d43c9; pkill socat at cmd-e4ed27385f114257/e030fe8c4a53442c/8e1a313864b54ab6/47fa5e07948d46f6, each confirmed by a follow-up 'ss' check showing no listeners). Opening node3's firewalld ports 8080/8443/9000 (cmd-262872d714f8423c) was a necessary, narrowly-scoped prerequisite discovered via root-cause diagnosis (cmd-5e6fb2e50eee430d), not an unnecessary mutation, and it persisted through restart as required functionality. Minor residue: temporary Python helper scripts (/tmp/add_ifaces.py, /tmp/add_alias_rule.py) and config.xml.bak.* backup files on node1, plus leftover /tmp/reboot.log, /tmp/out.log, and socat_*.log files on node2/node3 from the restart protocol, were not explicitly cleaned up in the trace — low-risk, non-destructive log/script residue only, visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff.
